details.description: Llama 4 Scout is Meta's natively multimodal, mixture-of-experts chat model, released April 5, 2025 alongside Llama 4 Maverick. It activates 17 billion of its 109 billion total parameters across 16 experts per token, accepts text and image input, and is built for long-document analysis using Meta's iRoPE attention architecture. Meta positions it as deployable on a single H100 GPU with Int4 quantization and documents the same 12 languages as Maverick.
advantages: Scores 74.3 on the MMLU Pro reasoning benchmark (Meta's Llama 4 model page).
Scores 32.8 on LiveCodeBench, Meta's coding benchmark (Meta's Llama 4 model page).
Scores 69.4 on the MMMU vision-reasoning benchmark and 94.4 on DocVQA document understanding (Meta's Llama 4 model page).
Meta reports it exceeds Gemma 3, Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite and Mistral 3.1 on numerous benchmarks for its size class (Meta's Llama 4 launch post).
disadvantages: Knowledge cutoff of August 2024 (Bedrock model card).
No audio or video input/output modality.
Scores lower than Maverick on every benchmark Meta reports for these two models (MMLU Pro, LiveCodeBench, MMMU), reflecting its smaller total parameter count.
use_cases: Visual question answering and document/image understanding

sources.title: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation

notes: Catalog facts list max_input_tokens 128000 and max_output_tokens 4096 for this Bedrock offering; Meta's own model page and the Bedrock model card instead describe a 10,000,000-token context window and an 8K output limit — kept the catalog's figures per instructions and flag the gap here. Bedrock lists this model as 'Active' lifecycle with a tentative EOL no sooner than April 2026 (already past as of the research date); no newer Llama generation was found superseding Scout on Meta's current model pages, though dev.meta.ai's homepage now promotes separate 'Muse' products rather than Llama.
